result.conclusion: Within the strict 30-minute planning window and basic crew profile (two 2-person general crews, 2 handtool_kits, 20 tie-downs, 1 cart, no specialists), at most two physical packages can be completed under upper-bound time estimates: one catch-basin surface clearing by general-1 (clear-inlet@report-16282611, 27 minutes max) and one window-latching package by general-2 (latch-windows@glass-1, 25 minutes max). Serial execution and upper-bound durations prevent either crew from completing a second task within 30 minutes. Compared with doing nothing, these two actions offer conditional, low-cost physical treatment of documented local failure mechanisms (surface drain clogging and open/unlatched operable windows), provided field conditions confirm actual defects and safe access. However, no calibrated damage-reduction model exists for either task, and if the target inlet is already clear or the windows are already latched, incremental physical benefit is zero.
result.why_not_do_nothing: Doing nothing expends zero labor and equipment, which avoids wasted effort if unconfirmed sites turn out to be inaccessible or already secure, and its storm loss is uncalibrated. However, doing nothing leaves all potentially active failure mechanisms untreated despite having two idle general crews and basic tools on hand. Storm evidence distinguishes several grades of justification: (1) local post-storm forensic investigation (SF DBI/WJE March 2023 glass report) identifying window hardware/condition and windborne debris as failure mechanisms; (2) external field investigations (FEMA P-942 after Sandy) showing real-storm operational benefits when backup pumps were connected to emergency power, alongside limiting failure conditions when floodgates were overtopped or transfer switches flooded, and FEMA Hurricane Michael observations showing opening protection alone does not preserve whole-building function; (3) external observational associations (UF/IFAS Hurricane Andrew study showing 73% vs 47% survival for properly pruned broad-leaved trees, which is non-causal and not a last-minute SF treatment effect); and (4) official operating guidance (SFPUC drain care, FEMA P-234 content moving and sandbagging). Deploying general-1 and general-2 on the two feasible tasks treats one flood-drainage mechanism and one wind-glazing mechanism within budget without fabricating quantified loss reductions.
result.remaining_gaps: Major operational and evidence gaps remain. First, all site conditions, permissions, and current defects are unchecked (`condition: unchecked`, `prerequisites_confirmed: false`); historical 311 locations and past glazing study addresses do not confirm current hazards, hydraulic connectivity, or operable window states. Second, 37 of 41 candidate packages are infeasible (`fits: false`) in this 30-minute basic scenario: Crew-1 and Crew-2 each can only complete one job because any second job's 20-to-25-minute upper work/setup duration plus `travel_between` exceeds the remaining 3 to 5 minutes. Third, all loose-item tie-down tasks (35–46 min max), content moves (85 min max), route clearances (49 min max), and 21 of 23 inlet-clearing sites (31–86 min max) exceed the 30-minute upper bound. Fourth, high-effort flood barriers, backup power, tree pruning, structural support, and traffic cordons cannot be accomplished due to missing specialist crews (electrician, arborist, building, traffic), unstaged equipment (0 pre-fitted barriers, 0 sandbags/fill, 0 pumps/circuits/electrical kits, 0 arborist kits, 0 engineered supports, 0 traffic sets), unestablished engineering designs/authority (`design_gap: true`), and multi-hour labor requirements (40 to 420 minutes). Finally, even if the selected tasks are completed, subsurface sewer capacity, coastal surge (0.5 m), power outages, tree failures, and structural wind loads remain completely unmitigated.

result.conclusion: Under the 480-minute planning window and specialist resource profile, the selected package deploys four distinct crews (electrician-1, arborist-1, general-1, general-2) to execute six conditional physical interventions while respecting all upper travel, setup, work-duration, and consumable stock limits. Arborist-1 uses 310 upper minutes (10 travel + 300 work/setup) to prune an assessed defect at report-16572155. General-1 walks to report-16239820 (100 Lombard St) and completes two co-located flood-protection tasks (fit-barrier and sandbag-wall) in 190 upper minutes (50 travel + 30 barrier + 0 travel_between + 110 sandbag wall). General-2 walks to glass-1 and then glass-2 to secure up to 20 total loose exterior items in 68 upper minutes (5 travel + 30 work/setup + 3 travel_between + 30 work/setup). All consumable stocks (1 pump, 1 backup_circuit, 1 fitted_barrier, 100 empty_sandbag, 1 sand_fill, and all 20 tie_down) are fully utilized without conflict, and both handtool_kits are used in parallel without waiting. The evidence base across these choices varies strictly by grade: backup-pump relies on an observed external storm outcome (FEMA P-942 in Hurricane Sandy); secure-items addresses a locally investigated failure mechanism (March 2023 SF DBI/WJE glazing study); fit-barrier reflects storm evidence of a limiting condition (overtopped floodgates in Sandy); prune-defect relies on an external observational association (73% vs 47% tree survival after Hurricane Andrew); and sandbag-wall rests on official guidance (FEMA P-234). result.why_not_do_nothing: Doing nothing expends zero labor minutes and commits no equipment, which avoids wasted effort if unconfirmed sites turn out to lack vulnerable items, defects, or compatible infrastructure. Neither doing nothing nor acting has a calibrated local loss or avoided-damage model—no cubic metres of water, percent risk reduction, or dollar savings can be claimed—but conditional physical work uses idle staged resources within their safe pre-storm operating window to interrupt specific, documented failure pathways before exposure begins.
result.remaining_gaps: Major operational and evidentiary gaps remain. First, two specialist crews (building-1 and traffic-1) cannot be used because their only candidate actions (engineered-support@glass-0 and install-cordon@report-16291635) have fits=false due to unestablished engineering design and traffic authority approval. Second, arborist-1 can only complete one pruning job because adding prune-defect@report-16572287 (300 min max work/setup + 31 min max travel_between) would require 641 upper minutes, exceeding the 480-minute limit. Third, because the schema caps selection at six packages, additional feasible general-crew actions—such as move-contents@report-16239820 (using the cart), latch-windows at glass sites, clear-route@report-16291635, and clearing the 21 mapped catch-basin inlets—must be left unselected. Fourth, all site observations (wind, trees, structure, flood, power, routes) are currently 'unchecked' with prerequisites_confirmed=false; historical 311 reports and owner survey addresses do not verify current defects, hydraulic connectivity, below-grate sewer capacity, owner permission, or hardware compatibility. Finally, no local experimental or quasi-experimental study quantifies the causal treatment effect or damage avoided per action in San Francisco.
